package lang // import "github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/pkg/lang"

Package lang reads source files and configuration into facts: symbols,
references, refused references and the facts a dialect declares, each with the
level that readings measured for the dialect that read it.

Bytes and a path go in. Nothing else is needed: no store, no daemon, no index,
no git and no network. A Reader is safe for concurrent use and deterministic:
equal inputs give byte-equal JSON, except where a time limit decides (a read
that overruns its deadline, a Reader that is busy).

The package is a door over fathom's own extraction code (ADR-092). Public
types are defined here, so a change inside fathom does not change this API.
Symbol.Canonical is a closed vocabulary that only grows; Symbol.Kind is each
dialect's own name and may change as a language improves.

Withheld values. A Result is not promised to carry no credential, but it
withholds the places one is found. The userinfo of a URL is dropped wherever
a string from the file lands (a name, a key, a reference target or its raw
spelling, an unresolved target, a fact), keeping an ssh account that has no
password and the image of a docker or oci reference; a userinfo ends at the
first '/', '?' or '#', so the host of a URL is never changed. A string literal
a Signature binds to a name or a key is masked as *** where it is a parameter's
default, a rule's value or a dictionary entry, and in every fact value.
The text of a script (a package.json or composer.json script, any task) is
not returned, only the program it runs, because a credential can sit in a
script in more shapes than a pattern covers. A credential flag (--password,
-u user:pass) and an Authorization header are masked in the rest of a Signature.
A credential in any other place (a name, a label, a literal that is an argument,
a block's own attributes) is returned as written.

Reading hostile input. Two boundaries, and each promises only what it can keep.
In process, Extract returns by a deadline (DefaultReadDeadline, lowered by
WithLimits): a read that overruns it is Incomplete, with one note naming the
deadline and none of its facts. Go cannot interrupt a goroutine, so the parser
is abandoned and keeps its CPU, and what it allocates, until it returns on its
own. Once GOMAXPROCS abandoned reads are running, Extract starts nothing more
and says SkipBusy. A fatal stack overflow, a parser that never returns and a
parser that allocates without bound end or starve the calling process whatever
the deadline says. The process boundary keeps those: cmd/fathom-lang reads in a
supervised child by default, kills it on an overrun, a death or a memory limit,
and the file in hand reads Incomplete while the batch continues. This package
starts no process, so a consumer that reads input it does not trust uses that
boundary.

Guards stay where nothing in process survives a failure: a parser that recurses
on nesting is handed no file nested past 10,000 levels, because a stack overflow
is fatal. A few parsers also refuse a shape that cost them hours (a run of
tokens no statement ends, a flood of lexical errors, a TOML document of 40,000
keys). A refused file reads Incomplete with the reason in Notes. No other shape
is promised refused or bounded in time or memory.

The wazero runtime that runs the grammars is process-wide, so its on-disk
compilation cache is a package function, EnableCompilationCache, and is off by
default. Without it the package writes no file.

CONSTANTS

const (
	PackEmpty      = "empty"      // the pack holds no dialect
	PackManifest   = "manifest"   // a manifest is unreadable or breaks the dialect rules
	PackConflict   = "conflict"   // an id, source kind, extension or basename is already taken
	PackEngine     = "engine"     // the engine is not tags or doc
	PackInjections = "injections" // queries.injections is not accepted in a pack
	PackGrammar    = "grammar"    // the grammar is not one the library embeds
	PackQuery      = "query"      // a query does not compile against its grammar
	PackContainer  = "container"  // match.container is not accepted in a pack
	PackClaims     = "claims"     // the dialect claims no file, claims one by a shebang, or names a glob that is not a pattern
	PackRoute      = "route"      // the dialect claims what a built-in dialect owns outright
)
    The reasons a pack or a Go extractor is refused, in PackError.Reason.
    The set is closed.

    The values are written as literals, not aliases of the internal constants,
    so a consumer reading the godoc sees them and a change to one is a visible
    edit here. TestPublicConstantValues holds them to the internal ones.

const (
	SkipBinary       = "binary"       // the bytes are not source text
	SkipOversize     = "oversize"     // over the file limit (2 MiB, lowerable by WithLimits)
	SkipGenerated    = "generated"    // a generated file the dialect excludes
	SkipAmbiguous    = "ambiguous"    // the file could belong to two dialects and the content does not settle it
	SkipUnclassified = "unclassified" // no dialect reads this path and content
	SkipNotLinked    = "not-linked"   // a dialect owns the file but its extractor is not linked into this Reader
	SkipBusy         = "busy"         // GOMAXPROCS reads past their deadline are still running, so this file was not started
)
    Skip reasons: the closed set Result.Skipped holds. A skipped file has no
    symbols; the reason says why.

const (
	LevelUnmeasured = "unmeasured" // no reading exists for the dialect
	LevelNone       = "none"       // measured, and no level was met
)
    Level values Result.Level and DialectInfo.Level hold besides L1 to L4.

const DefaultMaxFileBytes = 2 * 1024 * 1024
    DefaultMaxFileBytes is the largest file a Reader reads: the product's own
    limit, 2 MiB. A larger file is skipped as oversize. The value is a literal;
    TestPublicConstantValues holds it to the product's.

const DefaultReadDeadline = 30 * time.Second
    DefaultReadDeadline is how long Extract waits for one file: 30 seconds,
    above the budgets the tree-sitter engine spends on its own, so a file
    the engine would stop returns its own reason first. A read that passes it
    returns an Incomplete Result and abandons the parser, which keeps running
    until it returns (see Reader.Extract). WithLimits may lower it, never raise
    it. The value is a literal; TestPublicConstantValues holds it.


VARIABLES

var ErrClosed = errors.New("lang: reader is closed")
    ErrClosed is returned by Extract on a Reader that was closed.


FUNCTIONS

func EnableCompilationCache(dir string) error
    EnableCompilationCache turns on wazero's on-disk compilation cache for the
    process, under dir. It is off by default. The cache holds machine code the
    process will execute, so dir must be an absolute path that no group or
    other user can write and, on unix, that no other user owns (an owner can
    rewrite it whatever its mode); a directory that does not exist is created
    with mode 0700. It must be called before the first Reader is built, because
    the runtime is made once, and it errors on a second, different directory.
    Calling it again with the same directory is a no-op.


TYPES

type DialectInfo struct {
	ID string `json:"id"`
	// Kind is "language" or "tooling".
	Kind string `json:"kind"`
	// Engine is what reads the dialect: tags (a tree-sitter grammar and its
	// queries), doc (the document engine), tags+doc, or native (a Go reader
	// wired by hand, such as CMake, proto, nginx or Kubernetes). It is the
	// engine of the extractor the Reader dispatches to, which for a few
	// dialects is not the one their manifest declares.
	Engine string `json:"engine"`
	// Matches is the sorted extensions, basenames and globs the dialect claims.
	Matches []string `json:"matches"`
	// Level and Grade are what readings proved: Level is L1 to L4, LevelNone
	// or LevelUnmeasured, Grade the grade at that level ("" when none).
	Level string `json:"level"`
	Grade string `json:"grade"`
}
    DialectInfo describes one dialect a Reader can read.

type Extracted struct {
	Symbols    []Symbol
	References []Reference
	Unresolved []Unresolved
	Facts      []Fact
}
    Extracted is what an Extractor reads from one file. Symbol.Key,
    Symbol.Canonical and Reference.ToKey are derived by the Reader and ignored
    here. Reference.Edge is the extractor's own relation name and is passed
    through.

type Extractor interface {
	Extract(ctx context.Context, f File) (Extracted, error)
}
    An Extractor reads the files a Match claims. It must be safe for concurrent
    use and deterministic. A panic in it is returned by Reader.Extract as an
    error.

type Fact struct {
	// Entity is the Key of the symbol the fact belongs to, or the entity's name
	// when it is no symbol of this file.
	Entity string `json:"entity"`
	Key    string `json:"key"`
	Value  string `json:"value"`
	Line   int    `json:"line"`
}
    Fact is one scalar a dialect declares an entity writes.

type File struct {
	Path string
	Src  []byte
	// Siblings is the optional list of the other repository-relative paths in
	// the same repository. Some classifications read it (an Ansible role, a
	// Helm chart's templates, a Timoni module). Empty is legal: the file is
	// then classified alone, and Result.Notes says so when that could change
	// the verdict.
	Siblings []string
}
    File is one file to read. Path is repository-relative with forward slashes
    and is the only thing the Reader knows about where the file lives.

type Limits struct {
	// MaxFileBytes lowers the file size limit (DefaultMaxFileBytes).
	MaxFileBytes int
	// ReadDeadline lowers the time Extract waits for one file
	// (DefaultReadDeadline).
	ReadDeadline time.Duration
}
    Limits are the bounds a Reader works under. A zero field keeps the default.

type Match struct {
	// ID names the dialect: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and not a
	// dialect the Reader already has.
	ID string
	// Kind is "language" or "tooling" ("language" when empty).
	Kind string
	// Extensions (with their dot), Basenames and Globs claim files, as in a pack.
	// A built-in dialect's extension or basename is refused.
	Extensions []string
	Basenames  []string
	Globs      []string
	// Sniff claims files by content.
	Sniff *Sniff
	// Kinds maps each Symbol.Kind the extractor emits to its Symbol.Canonical,
	// a value of the closed vocabulary. At least one is required.
	Kinds map[string]string
}
    Match says which files a Go extractor reads and which kinds it emits.
    It is held to the rules a pack dialect is.

type Option func(*config) error
    Option configures New.

func Link(family string) Option
    Link adds an extractor family a sibling package registers by import, by its
    name. It is the hook pkg/lang/cue's Option calls, and cue is the only family
    there is: write cue.Option(), not Link("cue"). New returns an error when the
    family's package was not imported.

func WithDialects(fsys fs.FS) Option
    WithDialects adds a pack: dialects read from fsys, laid out as
    dialects/<id>/dialect.json beside the queries and doc specs each names.
    A pack is data. It names a grammar the library embeds and runs no code of
    its own, and only the "tags" and "doc" engines are accepted.

    The pack is merged with the built-in dialects and held to the same rules
    they are, then compiled, and New returns a *PackError and no Reader when any
    dialect breaks one. A pack dialect claims files by basename, glob or sniff,
    or by an extension no built-in dialect owns. It is tried after the specific
    built-in dialects and before an extension's generic reader, so it cannot
    take a file whose extension a built-in dialect owns, whatever its glob or
    basename says. Among the pack's dialects an exact basename claim beats a
    glob, a glob an extension, and equal claims go to the lower id. Its queries
    run under the same budget as the built-ins'. A pack dialect's Level is
    always LevelUnmeasured: no reading exists for it. queries.injections is not
    accepted in this version. A glob that is not a pattern, an empty tags query,
    a tags capture of a kind the manifest does not declare, a variant with
    its own tags query and no id, and a file in a dialect directory that the
    manifest does not name each refuse the pack.

    pkg/lang/langtest.CheckPack runs the same checks, then the pack's goldens.

func WithExtractor(m Match, e Extractor) Option
    WithExtractor registers a Go extractor under the same routing rules as a
    pack dialect: it is merged with the built-ins, tried (basename, then glob,
    then extension, then by id) after the specific built-ins and before an
    extension's generic reader, never for a file whose extension a built-in
    dialect owns, and refused whole, as a *PackError, when it breaks a rule. Its
    dialect appears in Dialects with Engine "native" and Level LevelUnmeasured.
    A context cancelled while the extractor runs is returned as the error.

func WithLimits(l Limits) Option
    WithLimits lowers the Reader's limits. A limit above the product's, or a
    negative one, is an error: no option raises a limit, and no option raises a
    grammar module's memory cap.

type PackError struct {
	// Reason is one of the Pack constants.
	Reason string
	// Dialect is the dialect that broke the rule, "" when the pack as a whole did.
	Dialect string
	// Detail says which rule and why.
	Detail string
}
    PackError is why New refused a pack or a Go extractor. Nothing of it is
    loaded: a pack is accepted whole or not at all.

func (e *PackError) Error() string

type Reader struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Reader reads files into facts. Build one with New and Close it. A Reader is
    safe for concurrent use.

func New(opts ...Option) (r *Reader, err error)
    New builds a Reader. It returns the error a bad option or a bad built-in
    dialect gives, and never panics. The Reader links every built-in dialect
    except CUE and Timoni, which a consumer adds by importing pkg/lang/cue.

func (r *Reader) Close() error
    Close releases the Reader's pooled grammar modules. It is idempotent, and
    waits for extractions in flight, but not for a parser an Extract abandoned
    at its deadline: that one runs until it returns on its own, its result
    discarded, and a grammar module it holds is released when it does.

func (r *Reader) Dialects() []DialectInfo
    Dialects lists every dialect the Reader reads, sorted by id, with the level
    and grade that readings measured for it.

func (r *Reader) Extract(ctx context.Context, f File) (Result, error)
    Extract reads one file. A file no dialect reads is not an error:
    the Result says why in Skipped. The error is for misuse (an empty path,
    a closed Reader, a done context). A file an extractor could not fully read
    returns what it did read, and Notes says what failed.

    Extract returns by a deadline (DefaultReadDeadline, lowerable by
    WithLimits). A read that overruns it returns Incomplete with one note naming
    the deadline and none of the facts it was reading. Go cannot interrupt a
    goroutine, so the parser is abandoned, not stopped: it keeps its CPU, and
    what it allocates, until it returns on its own, and its result is discarded.
    Once GOMAXPROCS abandoned reads are still running the Reader starts no more:
    Extract returns Skipped SkipBusy until some of them finish. A caller reading
    input it does not trust, where a parser may never return, reads through a
    process it can kill (cmd/fathom-lang does, by default). A context that ends
    first returns its error, and abandons the read the same way.

type Reference struct {
	// From is the Key of the referencing symbol, or "" for a reference the
	// document itself makes.
	From string `json:"from"`
	// To is the target as the dialect names it, with the userinfo of a URL
	// dropped (a withheld value, see the package documentation): a Go call names
	// package.Func, a Terraform reference var.name, a CloudFormation Ref the
	// logical id, a cross-file reference the path, image or address the
	// Strategy resolved. It is not necessarily a Key.
	To string `json:"to"`
	// ToKey is the Key of the symbol in the same file that To names, when To
	// equals exactly one symbol's Key or Name, and empty otherwise (a target
	// in another file, an ambiguous name, a cross-file reference).
	ToKey string `json:"to_key"`
	// Edge names the relation: "call" for a call by a code reader (Go, the
	// tree-sitter dialects, templ, Rego, notebooks), "reference" for a plain
	// reference from an engine that declares no relation, and
	// otherwise the edge the dialect declares (uses, imports, depends_on and
	// so on). Do not branch on an Edge across dialects.
	Edge string `json:"edge"`
	// Raw is the value as written, when it differs from To, with the userinfo of
	// a URL dropped.
	Raw string `json:"raw"`
	// Strategy is how a document reference resolved (repo-path, image-ref,
	// module-source and so on), empty for a call.
	Strategy string `json:"strategy"`
	// Line is the line the reference is written on. 0 means the engine does
	// not record one: calls read by the tree-sitter and Go engines carry no
	// line.
	Line int `json:"line"`
}
    Reference is one edge from a symbol (or the document, From "") to a target.

type Result struct {
	// Dialect is the id of the dialect or generic reader (generic-json,
	// generic-toml) that read the file, and "" only when nothing read it: a
	// skipped file. SkipNotLinked names the dialect that owns the file but is
	// not linked into this Reader.
	Dialect string `json:"dialect"`
	// Language is the file's language class from its path.
	Language string `json:"language"`
	// Skipped is a Skip reason, or "" when a dialect read the file.
	Skipped    string       `json:"skipped"`
	Symbols    []Symbol     `json:"symbols"`
	References []Reference  `json:"references"`
	Unresolved []Unresolved `json:"unresolved"`
	Facts      []Fact       `json:"facts"`
	// Level is the dialect's measured level: L1 to L4, LevelNone or
	// LevelUnmeasured. It is what readings proved about the dialect, not a
	// promise about this file. It is "" when Skipped is set: no dialect read
	// the file, so no level applies.
	Level string `json:"level"`
	// Incomplete is true when an engine could not fully read the file: the
	// symbols, references and facts above are what it did read, and Notes says
	// why. False means no engine reported a failure, which is not a promise
	// that every construct was read: the tree-sitter dialects recover from a
	// syntax error without reporting it, and the line scanners (CMake,
	// templ) have no failure concept. A policy tool that must not pass a file
	// it could not read should refuse when Incomplete is true.
	Incomplete bool `json:"incomplete"`
	// Notes disclose what the Reader could not know and that may have changed
	// the result. Empty when nothing did.
	Notes []string `json:"notes"`
}
    Result is what one file holds. Every slice is non-nil and sorted, so equal
    inputs give byte-equal JSON.

type Sniff struct {
	Extensions []string
	Pattern    string
}
    Sniff claims files of the listed extensions whose first kilobyte matches
    Pattern (a Go regular expression, matched across lines).

type Symbol struct {
	// Key is the symbol's identity within its file: Package and Name joined by
	// a dot, or Name alone when Package is empty. Reference.From and
	// Reference.ToKey hold Keys. A dialect names a reference target as it
	// writes it (Reference.To), which equals a Key only when the dialect
	// writes targets the way it names definitions; ToKey is the join.
	Key  string `json:"key"`
	Name string `json:"name"`
	// Package is the scope the extractor groups the symbol under, and the part
	// of Key before Name. It is the extractor's own scope, not a normalized
	// package: for most dialects it is the directory or package a definition
	// sits in, and for the Go extractor it is the package name for a function,
	// type, constant and variable but the receiver type for a method and the
	// owner type for a field (method M on type T reads Package "T", Name "T.M",
	// Key "T.T.M"). The scope is part of Key and so of Reference.From; it is
	// pinned by the tests and changes only as a Breaking change.
	Package string `json:"package"`
	// Kind is the dialect's own name for what the symbol is (for example
	// TerraformResource). Kinds may be added and renamed as languages
	// improve; do not branch on a Kind across dialects.
	Kind string `json:"kind"`
	// Canonical is the closed cross-dialect vocabulary. Values only grow. It
	// is empty for a kind that has no canonical meaning (a fact an extractor
	// observes, for example) and for a kind of an extractor no table maps. A
	// Go type reads struct, interface, type_alias (type A = B) or type (a
	// defined type such as type N int) by its declaration.
	Canonical string `json:"canonical"`
	Line      int    `json:"line"`
	// EndLine is the last line, 0 when the extractor does not compute it.
	EndLine   int    `json:"end_line"`
	Signature string `json:"signature"`
	// Tier is how the symbol was established: verified, pre-scan,
	// doc-claimed, sme-stated or assumed.
	Tier string `json:"tier"`
}
    Symbol is one definition.

type Unresolved struct {
	From   string `json:"from"`
	Edge   string `json:"edge"`
	Raw    string `json:"raw"`
	Reason string `json:"reason"`
	Line   int    `json:"line"`
}
    Unresolved is a reference the Reader read and refused to guess.
